Germany links Leipzig airport drone to people acting for Russian agencies

4 August 2026 · Leipzig/Halle Airport

Explosive-drone attack cluster; official state attribution

Overnight on 4–5 August 2026 a drone carrying professional explosives and a detonator reached Leipzig/Halle Airport at Schkeuditz, Germany, but the charge failed. The airport was disrupted. Separately, a cargo aircraft reported encountering an object in a suspected collision and diverted to Hanover; minor aircraft damage was reported, but the object was not conclusively identified as a drone. On 14 August a further suspected attack drone was found near Kabelsketal; the find was reported on 25 August, and the object was reportedly associated with about 50 g of suspected RDX.

On 1 September Germany attributed the operation to persons acting for Russian state agencies. Russia denied responsibility. The attribution has not been accompanied by public release of all the underlying forensic and intelligence evidence, and the launch point has not been established.

No casualties were reported. Police, bomb-disposal teams with a robot and federal prosecutors investigated, the additional device was seized, and diplomatic measures followed later.
